inputs.business_description: Natural gas mineral and royalty company; non-operated interests concentrated in the Marcellus Shale (Appalachian Basin) and Haynesville Shale (Haynesville Basin). Grew via the PHX Minerals acquisition (closed June 23, 2025) and the Three Rivers Royalty ("TRR") acquisition. [Fact, 424B4 pp. cover/Summary Reserve Data]
inputs.shares_class_a_at_ipo_close_source: 424B4 'Dilution' section: 15,296,579 Class A shares outstanding before offering as of 2026-05-26 (post Common Stock Reclassification) + 7,700,000 IPO shares = 22,996,579; 24,151,579 if underwriters' over-allotment option exercised in full. No 8-K/A found confirming over-allotment exercise as of 2026-08-05.
inputs.shares_class_b_source: 424B4 and 8-K Item 3.02: Class B common stock is paired 1:1 with WhiteHawk OpCo Interests issued to the Internalization sellers; no independent dividend/distribution rights.
inputs.shares_fully_diluted_as_converted_source: 424B4 'Dilution' table 'Assumed Redemption' basis: 18,638,633 Class A-equivalent before offering (post-Internalization, pre-offering) + 7,700,000 IPO shares = 26,338,633. Treats all Class B/OpCo Interests as redeemed 1-for-1 into Class A. Simple sum of 22,996,579 Class A + 3,750,000 Class B = 26,746,579 is a close but not identical alternate figure (small basis-date differences); use 26,338,633 as the filed number.
inputs.earnout_source: 8-K Item 2.01 and 424B4: up to 1,250,000 additional OpCo Interests/Class B shares (25% of the $130.0M Internalization Price) contingent on Adjusted EBITDA targets over three Earnout Years ending June 30, 2027 / 2028 / 2029. Progress toward EBITDA targets not yet disclosed.
inputs.cash_pro_forma_source: 424B4 Capitalization table, 'As Adjusted' column, as of 2026-03-31: cash and cash equivalents $10,537 thousand after giving effect to the Internalization, this offering, and use of proceeds (incl. Senior Notes paydown and Series D redemption).

inputs.preferred_series_d_status: Fully redeemed with IPO proceeds (0 shares as-adjusted); 8-K states redemption cost approximately $39.9 million aggregate ($1,000/share plus accrued dividends and minimum-return top-up); 424B4 book value pre-redemption was $37.030 million (difference is accrued dividends/premium).
inputs.income_statement_source: 424B4 'Prospectus Summary — Summary Historical and Pro Forma Condensed Consolidated Financial and Other Data' and 'Non-GAAP Financial Measures' reconciliation tables. Pro forma FY2025 net loss of $(32.330) million is dominated by one-time Internalization-related items (loss on extinguishment of debt $21.017M, pro forma management-fee true-up $21.795M) and is not a run-rate operating figure; Adjusted EBITDA and Cash Available for Distribution back these out and are the better owner-earnings proxies pending a dividend policy.
inputs.restatement_disclosure: [HUMAN REVIEW] On 2026-04-22 the company concluded its audited FY2025 consolidated financial statements could no longer be relied upon due to material accounting errors: (i) recording of management fees and (ii) misclassification of pre-closing-date and post-effective-date monies received related to acquisitions. Source: 424B4 'Prospectus Summary — Restatement' and 'Risk Factors'.

growth_explanation.mechanism: WhiteHawk is a natural gas mineral and royalty aggregator (non-operated interests in the Marcellus and Haynesville Shales) that has grown primarily through acquisition (PHX Minerals, closed 2025-06-23; Three Rivers Royalty). Pro forma FY2025 revenue of $89.2 million (giving full-year effect to both acquisitions) versus $9.5 million historical FY2024 shows the scale of inorganic growth; the mechanism has not been separated into organic (price/volume on existing acreage) versus acquisition-driven growth, and no forward acquisition pipeline or reinvestment runway has been disclosed.
growth_explanation.stress: [HUMAN REVIEW] Growth has been driven by two disclosed acquisitions rather than organic production growth on a constant asset base; a stress test needs the reserve decline curve (not yet modeled) to separate a maintenance case (existing PDP decline) from a growth case (further acquisitions, which are not committed capital).
